### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **28** documentable anchor(s).

**31** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ea62933c2239b4c35b675f6af7d6812e01173edc`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 51 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **24** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ea62933c2239b4c35b675f6af7d6812e01173edc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `63de9fdf9081a78e12897c8ff4ec3533af5c34c6` — the merge of head `fe4a965322d1a2b138f739200961c800daab4f94` into base `ea62933c2239b4c35b675f6af7d6812e01173edc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 63de9fdf9081a78e12897c8ff4ec3533af5c34c6 && git checkout 63de9fdf9081a78e12897c8ff4ec3533af5c34c6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ea62933c2239b4c35b675f6af7d6812e01173edc fe4a965322d1a2b138f739200961c800daab4f94 && git checkout -B drift-repro ea62933c2239b4c35b675f6af7d6812e01173edc && git merge --no-ff fe4a965322d1a2b138f739200961c800daab4f94

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ea62933c2239b4c35b675f6af7d6812e01173edc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ea62933c2239b4c35b675f6af7d6812e01173edc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

- New served read `GET /api/v1/auth/client-address` (`auth-plugin.ts`, mounted ahead of the catch-all, beside `GET /admin/client-address`): a public-surface widening. Right. The route row is in `AUTH_ROUTE_LEDGER` (objectstack-mount, server-only, tracker id in the comment and not in the note) and in the conformance pin's objectstack-mount list; the ledger note names the gate, the closed query set and `no-store` correctly against the code.
- Accept set of that read: the query set is closed and empty (`runClientAddressRead` refuses any parameter `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` through `unknownQueryParamRefusalMessage`, before `trustsForwardedHeaders` is asked); no body. Right, and pinned (`?userId`, `?organizationId`, `?address`).
- Its gate (`judgeOrganizationAddressReader`, `client-address-read.ts`): no principal 401 UNAUTHENTICATED; a held posture 403 with the posture's code; no `setup.write` in `systemPermissions` 403 PERMISSION_DENIED. Read against the cited code: `resolveOrganizationSettingsCaller` passes the settings door's exact parameter set (`settings-service-plugin.ts:493-508`: fail-closed, `authGate: 'resolved'`, api-key-and-session, sessionApi optional, session request, localization/accessToken withheld), differing only in the tenancy resolver (the plugin's own `TenancyService` instead of the kernel lookup; both satisfy `TenancyServiceResolver`, and `null` reads as no posture). `judgeHeldSession({ authGate })` reaches `normalizeAuthGate`, which reads `.authGate.code` against the closed vocabulary, so the held arm works on the resolved `AuthGate`. `setup.write` is declared `scope: 'org'` in `capabilities.ts` and lands in `systemPermissions`; the settings door's union with `permissions` is defensive, not a gap. Right.
- `GET /api/v1/auth/client-address` on a store outage: `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` is relayed `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` in the shared seam's words. Right. An `ApiKeyLifecycleRefusalError` (a revoked, expired or inactive key, which `resolveRequestExecutionContext` propagates and `credentials: 'api-key-and-session'` reaches) falls to the generic `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` arm and an error log line, where the settings door relays `err.status`/`err.code` (`settings-routes.ts:175`). Fail-closed, so not a disclosure, but a wrong status class: should-fix S1 below.
- D3, `customSession` door (`auth-manager-plugin-list.ts`): `ctx?.request ? { address: readRequestClientAddress() } : await readMountDoor()`. A better-auth-served read keeps the request door; an in-process read at an objectstack mount takes the mount door; a programmatic read with no door open still judges limits only. Right. `enforceSessionControls` judges the list only when `door && organizationId && allowedIpRanges.length > 0`, ends the session `ip_not_allowed`, and `judgeSessionScopingAddress` admits a platform admin regardless. The `{ address: undefined }` door is refused under a set list, which is D5's own rule for an unestablishable address.
- Mount middleware (`auth-plugin.ts` `rawApp.use(basePath/*)`): registered after the D5 gate and the agent-forward middleware and before every `rawApp.get`, so it wraps every raw route and the catch-all. The catch-all's `handleRequest` still opens its own fresh `runWithRequestState(new WeakMap(clientAddressStateEntries(address)))` (`auth-manager-request-routing.ts:190`), so the sign-in address stamp and the HTTP door's slot are undisturbed by the outer door. The in-process `auth.api.getSession` reusing the open store is not something I could read from better-auth's source (this clone carries no `node_modules`); it is pinned on a real better-auth instance by `organization-access-policy-doors.test.ts` (red-first 12, ablation 2 red), which is the right pin for a vendor-internal dependency.
- D1: `sys_session.revoke_reason` description names `ip_not_allowed`; six `*.objects.generated.ts` bundles carry the same insertion (en regenerated, five hand-edited identically). Right; the generated files are not reviewed beyond that read.
- D2: `POST /organization/set-active` pinned on the real route: 401, `idle_timeout`, scope unchanged, `last_activity_at` unchanged; control 200. Right.
- S6 narrowing: `console.organizationMfa.needsTwoFactor` and `.nowRequired` leave all eleven packs; `organizationMfaNotices.ts`, its test, the `AppContent.tsx` call, the `findOne` of the stored column and the save-toast `description` spread are gone; the de-quote census moves 110 to 109. `git grep organizationMfa` on the head finds no remaining reader outside the two changesets and the census comments. `organizationMfaNotices.ts` was not exported from `@object-ui/app-shell`'s index, so app-shell's change is internal. Right.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/31030-org-admin-client-address.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` patch (a new route, `Metadata-protocol: none`, so patch per the kind rule), `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch (a description string), `@object-ui/i18n` patch with the BREAKING banner (a non-protocol narrowing ships patch and keeps its banner), `@object-ui/app-shell` patch (an internal module removed). Right for what the diff publishes.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset, line-initial; the title carries `!`; the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (runtime-interface-only ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts#TranslationKeys)` is present and `Check Changeset` (the job that runs `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base`) is green; the migration table maps both removed keys to their replacement (none, with the reason). The seat's claim amendment 6710714517 already settled `widening` to `narrowing`; the declaration matches the diff against `main`.
- One accuracy point: `.changeset/30295-org-mfa-notice-and-enroll-refusal.md`, which ADDED these two keys, is still pending on this head and `@object-ui/i18n`'s CHANGELOG (18.3.0) does not carry them, so no released pack ever had them. The body's sentence "the published packs drop" over-states a consumer-visible break; the declaration is conservative relative to `main` and follows the 30206 precedent, so it stands. Should-fix S2 (wording only).

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none` in the dev report: no flags to answer. `premise_still_valid: true` holds (#30922 closed; D1-D3 re-checked and done, see ①).
- Out-of-scope 1 (boundary flake in `organization-access-policy.test.ts`, strict `>` at exactly 60 minutes): carried by #31175, which holds that file; correctly not touched here.
- Out-of-scope 2 (the console's Access policy page does not read the new route; consumer none): the card's acceptance asked for the served read and the plain-member refusal, both delivered; the route is not a declared-and-undelivered capability. The carrier is `none` though. Should-fix S3: file the follow-up card so the seam named in Acceptance notes has an owner.
- Out-of-scope 3 (`content/docs` teaches no per-organization access policy): a docs gap predating this card; noted, not a condition here.
- Deviations: a new test file because #31175 holds the sibling, accepted; no labels on `pr_create` because the order names none and the relay refuses an empty list, accepted; `origin/main` merged once after #31194 with the census conflict resolved to 109, accepted (the head is that merge); assignees followed the order over os-dev.md rule 2, a seat process point for the order's author, not this record; #30974's claim surface read before touching `AppContent.tsx`, accepted.
- The PR body's Acceptance notes carry no further flag. Nothing to escalate.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`. `sys_organization.require_mfa` is declared `readonly: true`, labelled retired, its description sends the author to Settings → Access policy, and the D2 guard strips a user-context write (`sys-organization.object.ts:413-432`); ADR-0069 as amended 2026-11-06 puts the requirement in `access_policy.mfa_required` with three levels, whose save refusal (`organization-mfa-enrollment-guard.ts`, `ORGANIZATION_MFA_REFUSAL_COPY`) already names two-factor itself. A form notice over a column no form can write serves no reader, so removing it makes the spec's own retirement real at the consumer; it takes no declared capability away. The card's Expected S6 allowed "removed, or re-pointed", the seat ruled removal, and the migration table says why neither key has a replacement. The removal breaks no compile (`t()`'s key is a `string`; `TranslationKeys` is `typeof en`, re-exported from `@object-ui/i18n` and `@object-ui/react`, and no workspace consumer names the two keys). Holds.

The new read, tried as an attacker. Who may call: any principal a session or API key admits whose `systemPermissions`, resolved for the session's VETTED active organization, hold `setup.write`. `grantAppliesInTenant` applies a grant row only in the organization it names, a caller with no active organization gets no stored grant at all, and an organization claim the membership no longer backs is dropped and re-resolved (`resolve-authz-context.ts:797-815`), so a member cannot borrow another organization's `setup.write` by claiming it; the only way in is to BE an administrator of the organization the session is scoped to, which is the caller the save check admits. A platform administrator is admitted only through `setup.write`, never through the admin anchor (the dogfood pin shows the converse: an organization administrator is still refused at `/admin/client-address`). What it discloses: the caller's own connection's judged address, and `trustProxy`. The address was already disclosed to this caller by the save refusal's `constraint.clientAddress`; `trustProxy` was platform-admin-only before and is now readable by every organization administrator, but it is a boolean the same caller can already infer by comparing the save refusal's address against a forwarded header, and it is needed to read the answer at all behind a proxy; acceptable, and judged. Can it answer for another organization or user: there is no parameter of any kind, the query set is closed before the address is read (pinned on three names), and the answer is a transport fact of THIS connection, so there is nothing organization-scoped to redirect; the organization enters only through the gate. `Cache-Control: no-store` keeps one connection's answer off a shared cache. The route sits under both the D5 deployment gate and the new mount door, so a caller already outside a list in force is refused or ended before the read; a caller whose session is held is refused with the posture's code before any address is read (pinned, `trustsForwardedHeaders` not called). The 500 arm returns a generic message, which is tighter than the platform route's `err.message`. No must-fix.

D3 design, tried against the spec: TL;DR 6 and D5 say the organization's list is judged on login/session at the auth mount with the one trust rule, and an unestablishable address is refused while any range is set. The mount door carries `resolveClientAddress` under the same `trustProxy` rule the D5 gate just applied, opens `{ address: undefined }` when none is established, and leaves no door outside the auth mount, so data requests are judged by neither list as before. The one risk I looked for, the outer door shadowing or being shadowed by `handleRequest`'s own store, does not arise: `handleRequest` opens a fresh store with the address entries, and `customSession` there has `ctx.request`. The design holds as implemented; the dependency on better-auth reusing an open store for in-process endpoint calls is pinned on the real instance, which is the right place for it.

Findings:
- S1 (should-fix): `GET /api/v1/auth/client-address` answers an `ApiKeyLifecycleRefusalError` with `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` and an error log line; relay it as the settings door does (`err.status`, `err.code`, `err.message`) beside the 503 arm, and pin one case (a revoked key).
- S2 (should-fix, wording): the changeset's narrowing sentence says the published packs drop the two keys; they were added by the still-pending `.changeset/30295-...md` and never released, so say so, or the CHANGELOG will read as a consumer-visible break in the same version that adds them.
- S3 (should-fix, outside the diff): file the follow-up card for the console's Access policy page to read the new route; the dev's seam has `carrier: none`.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-em08na`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5p3T5YWhLjurajudnQ`

**VERDICT: PASS**

Seat disposition of the should-fixes: S2 (changeset wording, prose only) goes to the dev now; S1 (the revoked-key status on the new read, a code change that would re-open this narrowing review and the dogfood battery) and S3 (the console Access policy page reading the new route) are filed as follow-up cards before ACCEPT.
